findings.claim: the ov-dash stop was not recorded where later tickets see it
the test did not assert the master.toml mount
the summary still said SeaweedFS is planned

minio-removal step 6 offers `nomad job eval ov-dash` as a way to start the stopped job, but evaluating a job with Stop=true places nothing; only a re-register (an applications-root apply or nomad job run) starts it

verdict.text: f1 and f3 are fixed, and f2 is resolved as well.
One new non-blocking finding, f4: the restart step in the minio-removal plan names a command that does not start a stopped job.
The other option on the same line, an applications-root apply, does start it, and step 1A applies that root before step 6 anyway.
So the outcome still holds, but the wording should be corrected.

Gates: I ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree myself: `pass gate pre_commit`, `pass gate cli_tests`, `pass eval-row r1`, `stamp green: 1b9c6ca89fa6a0d8a4f070ba967a60af4541696a701fcabca0fedf2ef75c1f47`.

f1: `.okf/components/ov-dash.md` has a new section that says when and why ov-dash stopped, that it holds no state, that minio-removal restarts it, and that applications-root applies in the meantime queue it.
The orangepi4a jobs table marks the row stopped until minio-removal, adds the seaweedfs row, and adds a quirk entry.
`.okf/components/seaweedfs.md` agrees.
The minio-removal plan (main checkout) has step 6 and an outcome bullet saying ov-dash runs healthy and answers on its route.
That is the documented-handoff option from round 1, not the Terraform option, which is fine.
f3: the summary line now says SeaweedFS runs beside MinIO and is replacing it, and notes that ov-dash is stopped.
f2: `test_master_toml_is_mounted_where_weed_reads_it` asserts both the template destination and the exact volume mount string.
f1 (resolved): recorded in ov-dash.md, orangepi4a.md, seaweedfs.md and minio-removal step 6 plus its outcome bullet.
f2 (resolved): the mount test is at cli/tests/test_seaweedfs_jobspec.py:58.
f3 (resolved): .okf/summary.md has been updated.
f4 (docs, non-blocking): `nomad job eval` on a stopped job asks the scheduler to evaluate a job whose desired state is stopped, so it places nothing.
Step 6 should say to re-register the job (an applications-root apply, or `nomad job run`).
If step 1A's apply has already re-registered it, the queued allocation places by itself once MinIO's memory is freed.
This is a plain wording fix and does not need another review.
The ov-dash.md text calls a re-registered ov-dash a queued allocation, and that matches how Nomad blocks an eval that cannot place.
The SSH host-key note from round 1 is now a quirk entry on the orangepi4a page.
